graph.title: Squidman Escape
notes: The manual's inventory (p.14) provides Element IDs; none were in the catalogue, so every part type is new (lego-<Element ID>). Port names are generic (stud.N / anti-stud.N) since exact stud positions are not itemised; each stud/anti-stud port is used once.
The inventory lists the green Squidman legs as '74040', which is not a valid part number (probably truncated in the scan), so the type is named lego-legs-green rather than inventing an ID.
Stickers (POLICE x2, police badge, decals) are not counted as parts. The badge sticker is assumed to be on the white flag piece 4523403.

Element-to-picture matching is a best guess from small thumbnails: b2 (rear fingers) and b11 (top clip plate) could be swapped between 4140583 and 4515337; 4140583 appears 3x in the inventory, the third copy (b40) is placed on the side plate of the tail sub-assembly (page 10 step 5) with low confidence.

Tail sub-assembly (pages 9-10): the red 2x2 plate sits on the underside of the black 2x2 after flipping (step 3); the 1x4 side plates and small wedges attach to its sides. It hinges onto the rear fingers of the main body at step 11 (hinge/hinge).
Steps 7-8 wedges attach to the grey 2x4 plate and sit against the white bricks; only the grey-plate stud join is recorded.

The booklet really builds two separate models: the police ship with its pilot (pages 3-11), and the Squidman villain minifig (page 2), who is assembled on his own, stands apart from the ship, and is never attached to it. The two groups are therefore intentionally left unconnected (no joined or contact edge is shown or implied in the manual). The cape sits on the torso neck stud and the head is mounted on top of the cape, modelled as torso neck -> cape anti-stud, cape stud -> head.
The police minifig is seated on the grey plate (step 12) with a hand on the steering handle; the visor hinges on the black helmet.

graph_initial.title: Squidman Escape
notes: The manual's inventory (p.14) provides Element IDs; none of them were in the catalogue, so every part type is new (lego-<Element ID>). Port names are generic (stud.1 / anti-stud.1) since exact stud positions are not itemised.
Stickers (POLICE x2, police badge, wing/stripe decal sheets) are not counted as parts. The badge sticker is assumed to be on the white flag piece 4523403.

Element-to-picture matching is a best guess from small thumbnails: b2 (rear fingers) and b11 (top clip plate) could be swapped between 4140583 and 4515337; 4140583 appears 3x in inventory, the third copy (b40) is placed on the side plate of the tail sub-assembly (page 10 step 5) with low confidence.

Tail sub-assembly (pages 9-10): the red 2x2 plate sits on the underside of the black 2x2 after flipping (step 3); the 1x4 side plates and the two small wedges attach to its sides. It clips onto the rear fingers of the main body at step 11.

Steps 7-8 wedges attach to the grey 2x4 plate and sit against the white bricks; only the grey-plate stud join is recorded. The police minifig is seated on the grey plate (step 12) with a hand on the steering handle; the Squidman minifig stands separately holding the money tile (page 2).
Minifig assemblies on page 2 and step 12 are included as joined edges; the visor hinge is on the black helmet.
